title: The Collapse That Will Change A Generation - Ray Dalio's Warning For 2025 & World War 3 Odds
summary: Ray Dalio describes his big-cycle model of debt, internal conflict and a rising rival, raises his odds of US civil war and a US-China conflict, and gives inflation-era investing advice.

assertions.quote: Usually the coffers are empty, they're printing a lot of money and then they're trying to use uh economics as a weapon.

verdicts.note: Debt and inequality often precede internal turmoil, but historians find no reliable pattern linking them to great-power war; the big cycle rests on a selective reading of a few empires.

assertions.quote: And that historically is when a rising power makes its move.
So you're seeing those sides line up and all sides are in preparation for war.
you give a 30% chance of the US falling into civil war, I think in the next 5 to 10 years

verdicts.note: Polarisation and political violence are rising, but forecasters and scholars put an organised US civil war far below one in three.
CFR's experts rate growing political violence and unrest in the US as high-likelihood and high-impact for 2026, which is a serious risk of violence, not of civil war.

assertions.quote: The capital wars um are the ones that accelerate immediately before um the uh the military wars.

verdicts.note: The 1941 oil embargo preceded Pearl Harbor, but many heavy sanctions regimes, on Iran, Cuba or the USSR, never led to great-power war.

In the case file, US sanctions and the August 1941 oil embargo on Japan were the 'final straw' before Pearl Harbor. That is one strong case of economic war just before a shooting war, but the file does not show it is the usual sequence.

assertions.quote: The world is lining up which you know, there are in wars typically acts axis and next and allied powers.

verdicts.note: Russia, China, Iran and North Korea cooperate more and Western alliances have tightened, but much of the world, such as India and the Gulf states, stays non-aligned.

Asked about the global order in 10 years, 68% of the WEF's experts expect a multipolar or fragmented order and only 14% a bipolar order of two superpowers. Fragmentation is widely expected, but a two-bloc split is the minority view.

assertions.quote: And so we don't have a dominant military power anymore.

verdicts.note: The US still has the largest military and global reach, but China now rivals it in the Western Pacific and Russia matches it in nuclear weapons.
The US share of world spending fell to a third and its lead over China narrowed from 3.2 to 2.8 times, but it still outspends every rival by far; spending is not capability.

CSIS quotes the USCC: PLA advances have 'fundamentally transformed the strategic environment', weakening deterrence in the Strait; the report adds that China still lags the US in quality and breadth of capability.
DDIS says China's military strength in the Western Pacific is already roughly on a par with the US and the balance will shift further its way; that is regional, not global.

assertions.quote: in weaponizing the dollar um it is leading those to get around and not want to hold dollars

verdicts.note: Central banks have shifted some reserves into gold since 2022, but the dollar's share of reserves has fallen only slowly.

assertions.quote: we are in the first four of those wars um in in this competition.

verdicts.note: Calling tariffs, export controls and rivalry for influence 'wars' is framing.

The WEF report describes trade disruption at its most severe in decades, sanctions and export controls spreading to AI, chips, quantum and rare earths, and pressure on countries not aligned with China or the US. It treats capital-flow conflict as a possible future front (L1372-L1373), not one under way.
